item.title: DePaul blocks Students for Justice in Palestine until 2027
item.description: The pro-Palestinian club at DePaul University is facing sanctions for its repeated social media posts.

item.title: New Virginia AG moves to defend in-state tuition for illegal immigrants
item.description: New Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones is defending a law allowing illegal immigrants to qualify for in-state tuition and financial aid. Jones aims to defend Virginia’s law against a lawsuit from the Department of Justice, which claims such laws discriminate against U.S. citizens.

item.title: Law professor dissects lawsuit against WSU by families of four murdered Idaho students
item.description: 'This guy was harassing women. He was stalking women. He was a general creep. … Could they have foreseen that he might harass somebody?'

item.title: An in-depth discussion with the professor who just won a major free speech victory
item.description: The 9th Circuit Court of Appeals held that Professor Reges' syllabus was protected by the First Amendment.

item.title: Is Plato really cancelled? Texas A&M syllabus review policy stirs debate
item.description: Texas A&M University's new policy banning classroom advocacy for race and gender ideology has sparked controversy after a philosophy professor was told to remove one of Plato’s works from his syllabi.

item.title: Despite ‘institutional neutrality,’ Columbia journalism school condemns Trump
item.description: Institutional neutrality remains an elusive promise, even to the schools that pledge support.
